reviewer: Graeham C. Gillin (Charleston, SC bar) — already the live byline; keep
sourceNotes: Primary sources read directly: scstatehouse.gov chapters t15c003, t15c038, t15c051, t15c078, t61c002, t61c004, t61c006 (downloaded 2026-09-25); SCDPS South Carolina Traffic Collision Fact Book 2024 Edition, Charleston County pages 104-105 and county rankings (PDF downloaded); SCDOT SC 171 Folly Road Safety Audit public-information handout (May 22, 2025) and Board 1 crash-history display (PDFs downloaded from info2.scdot.org); BCDCOG Rethink Folly Road Complete Streets Study Appendix (Feb 2016, PDF); BCDCOG Riverland Corridor Management Plan (PDF); Town of James Island Comprehensive Plan 2021 (PDF); sccourts.org circuit map. charleston-sc.gov and charlestoncounty.gov refused every direct connection this session (TLS reset / socket closed), so the two City pages and the County release cited below were read only through search-index snippets of those URLs; each is marked 'snippet' in its note. Sibling packs reused: facts-4729 (dram-shop / 2025 Act No. 42 analysis), facts-4738 and facts-4355 (Tort Claims Act, SOL, Nelson URL).

verifiedClaims.claim: Folly Road (SC-171) is the lifeline of James Island — and the primary route to Folly Beach
verifiedClaims.currentValue: Folly Road is SC 171. The Town of James Island's Comprehensive Plan (2021) calls it 'the main access route through the island' and 'a key five lane wide artery, connecting James Island with the West Ashley areas of Charleston to the north and to the town of Folly Beach to the south'; the BCDCOG study describes the bridges over the Folly River as the only road onto Folly Beach.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: Town of James Island Comprehensive Plan 2021, ch. 3.7 (Folly Road Improvements); SCDOT SC 171 Folly Road Safety Audit handout
verifiedClaims.note: Route designation and role verified. The 'Folly Beach' anchor points at the Charleston office page (/locations/south-carolina/charleston/); there is no Folly Beach location page (/locations/south-carolina/charleston/folly-beach/ falls through to the Charleston page). Not a factual error, but the anchor promises a page that does not exist; see recommendedEdits.

verifiedClaims.claim: According to the South Carolina Department of Public Safety, the Folly Road corridor consistently ranks among the most dangerous roads in Charleston County for traffic collisions.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: SCDPS publishes no such ranking. The 2024 Traffic Collision Fact Book's Charleston County page lists the county's top five roadways by collisions as US-17 (1,805), I-26 (1,213), US-52 (1,140), I-526 (585) and US-78 (534); SC-171 does not appear, and the county's top five intersections are all on I-26. The attribution is invented. What is sourced: SCDOT's Office of Traffic Safety selected the Folly Road corridor (Maybank Highway to Old Folly Beach Road, about five miles) for a federal Highway Safety Improvement Program road safety audit after it recorded 2,103 vehicular, 15 pedestrian and 21 bicycle crashes from January 2018 to December 2022, 525 of them injury crashes and 6 fatal. County-wide, Charleston County logged 15,802 collisions in 2024 (57 fatal, 62 killed, 3,521 injury collisions) — second in the state for total collisions and first for serious-injury collisions.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: SCDOT, SC 171 Folly Road Safety Audit public information meeting handout (May 22, 2025); SCDPS Traffic Collision Fact Book 2024 Edition, Charleston County pp. 104-105 and county rankings
verifiedClaims.note: Suggested: 'The South Carolina Department of Transportation selected the five-mile stretch of Folly Road between Maybank Highway and Old Folly Beach Road for a federally funded road safety audit after it recorded 2,103 vehicle crashes, 15 pedestrian crashes and 21 bicycle crashes between January 2018 and December 2022 — 525 of them causing injury and six of them fatal. Charleston County as a whole logged 15,802 collisions in 2024, second in South Carolina, and led the state in serious-injury collisions (SCDPS Traffic Collision Fact Book 2024).' Keep the scdps.sc.gov link (the host is on the outbound allowlist); the Fact Book PDF URL is in authoritativeLinks.

verifiedClaims.claim: the bottleneck effect of being the only road to Folly Beach
verifiedClaims.currentValue: Folly Road is the sole road access to Folly Beach: the corridor narrows to one lane in each direction through the conservation area and crosses the rebuilt Folly River bridges (one lane each way) onto Center Street.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: BCDCOG, Rethink Folly Road Complete Streets Study, Appendix (Feb. 2016), urban design analysis

verifiedClaims.claim: Folly Road runs roughly seven miles from the James Island Connector (SC-30) near downtown Charleston to the entrance of Folly Beach.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: The City of Charleston and the Town of James Island both measure the James Island segment at 7.87 miles between the Wappoo Cut Bridge and Center Street on Folly Beach. The Connector's junction with Folly Road sits south of the Wappoo Cut Bridge, so 'roughly seven miles' from the Connector to Folly Beach is consistent.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: Town of James Island Comprehensive Plan 2021 ('The 7.87 mile segment of Folly Road between Center Street on Folly beach and the Wappoo Cut Bridge'); City of Charleston, Rethink Folly Road page (same 7.87-mile figure; snippet)
verifiedClaims.note: Optional tightening: 'about eight miles from the Wappoo Cut Bridge to Center Street on Folly Beach (7.87 miles by the City of Charleston's measure)'.

verifiedClaims.claim: Much of Folly Road is a four-lane divided highway with a center turn lane
verifiedClaims.currentValue: It is not divided. Through James Island, Folly Road is a five-lane section — two travel lanes in each direction and a continuous center turn lane — that transitions to one lane in each direction through the conservation area and across the bridges to Folly Beach. The raised medians SCDOT proposed in its safety audit were contested precisely because the road has no median today.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: BCDCOG Rethink Folly Road Appendix ('five vehicular lanes (two in each direction and a center turn lane)'); BCDCOG Riverland Corridor Management Plan ('a five-lane urban arterial' at North Grimball Road); Town of James Island Comprehensive Plan 2021 ('a key five lane wide artery')
verifiedClaims.note: Suggested: 'Through James Island, Folly Road is a five-lane road — two travel lanes each way and a continuous center turn lane, with no median — that narrows to one lane in each direction on the marsh approach to Folly Beach.'

verifiedClaims.claim: During peak beach season, traffic can back up for miles, and travel times that should take 10 minutes stretch to an hour or more.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: No source gives a 10-minute-to-an-hour figure. What is sourced: 'On weekends in the spring and summer beach season, daytime traffic is impacted by residents and tourists making their way to and from Folly Beach' (Town comp plan), and BCDCOG traffic counts put Folly Road's 2019 average daily traffic at 33,000 at Harbor View Road, 29,800 at Fort Johnson Road and 16,600 at Grimball Road.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: Town of James Island Comprehensive Plan 2021, ch. 3.7 and Figure 3.7.1 (James Island Area Traffic Counts, 2013-2019, BCDCOG data)
verifiedClaims.note: Suggested: 'Folly Road carried about 33,000 vehicles a day at Harbor View Road and nearly 30,000 at Fort Johnson Road in 2019 (BCDCOG counts), and on spring and summer weekends beach traffic backs up on top of that.' Drop the 10-minutes/hour sentence.

verifiedClaims.claim: Unlike most major roads in the Charleston area, Folly Road has essentially no parallel alternative. If you live on James Island or want to reach Folly Beach, you are on Folly Road.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: Overstated for James Island: Riverland Drive runs parallel to Folly Road (BCDCOG wrote a whole Riverland Corridor Management Plan because it functions as the alternative route), and Harbor View Road, Camp Road and Maybank Highway also move island traffic. Accurate for Folly Beach, which has no other road access.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: BCDCOG, Riverland Corridor Management Plan (Riverland Drive serves as the parallel route; Central Park Road lets drivers avoid 'the often-congested Maybank Highway/Folly Road intersection'); BCDCOG Rethink Folly Road Appendix
verifiedClaims.note: Suggested: 'Folly Road is the only road on and off Folly Beach, and on James Island the parallel routes — Riverland Drive, Harbor View Road, Camp Road — are two-lane neighborhood streets that cannot absorb its volume. Beach traffic, commuters, school buses, commercial vehicles and cyclists all end up on the same five lanes.'

verifiedClaims.claim: During summer months, a significant percentage of drivers on Folly Road are tourists who do not know the road
verifiedClaims.currentValue: No percentage is stated, and none exists; the tourist-traffic characterization is supported by the Town's plan ('Many of the businesses along Folly Road cater to the needs of tourists traveling to the beach'; weekend beach-season traffic).
verifiedClaims.sourceName: Town of James Island Comprehensive Plan 2021
verifiedClaims.note: Keep as written; do not add a number.

verifiedClaims.claim: Left turns across traffic into businesses and shopping centers are a primary cause of T-bone collisions on Folly Road.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: SCDOT's stated reason for proposing raised medians on Folly Road: 'The raised medians are designed to manage access and promote safer movements at existing signals. They aim to limit left turns from certain properties, as angle collisions tend to result in the most severe accidents' (Shawn Salley, SCDOT program manager); 'concrete medians ... help prevent those angled crashes that end up in injuries and fatalities' (Ginny Jones, SCDOT). Countywide, 'Failed To Yield Right of Way' was the most-listed contributing factor in Charleston County in 2024 (3,525 listings, 8 in fatal collisions).
verifiedClaims.sourceName: Count On 2 (WCBD), 'Local leaders set to discuss updates on Folly Road safety improvements' (May 13, 2025); WCIV, 'James Island residents share thoughts on Folly Road improvement project' (May 22, 2025); SCDPS Fact Book 2024, Charleston County contributing factors
verifiedClaims.note: Optionally attribute: 'SCDOT's own safety audit targeted these angle crashes with raised medians because, in its words, they "end up in injuries and fatalities".'

verifiedClaims.claim: Folly Road's speed limit changes multiple times along its length — from 45 mph in some sections to 35 mph in commercial areas to 25 mph approaching Folly Beach.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: Verified: 45 mph on the five-lane James Island section (posted 45 at North Grimball Road; a 2015 speed study reduced the corridor's former 50 mph section to 45). BCDCOG's 2015 inventory found 'Speeds range between 40-50 MPH along the corridor, except within the core of Folly Beach where 30 MPH is posted'; in June 2018 SCDOT approved Folly Beach's request to post 25 mph within city limits. No source supports a 35 mph commercial zone.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: BCDCOG Riverland Corridor Management Plan (45 mph at N. Grimball Rd); BCDCOG Rethink Folly Road Appendix B (speed inventory; 50-to-45 reduction); WCIV, 'Folly Beach gets DOT approval to lower speed limit to 25 mph' (June 6, 2018)
verifiedClaims.note: Suggested: 'Folly Road is posted at 45 mph across most of James Island, then drops sharply on the approach to Folly Beach, where the city won SCDOT approval in 2018 to post 25 mph inside its limits. Drivers who carry 45 mph into the two-lane marsh section or onto Center Street create the speed differentials behind many rear-end crashes.'

verifiedClaims.claim: Folly Road is a popular cycling route (it connects to the Folly Beach bike path)
verifiedClaims.currentValue: There is no 'Folly Beach bike path'. Folly Road carries on-street bike lanes along portions of the corridor, with gaps ('Bike lanes are not included in a few critical areas, making cycling difficult'), and the rebuilt bridges to Folly Beach 'include bike lanes and sidewalks'. The county's Rethink Folly Phase 1 (Ellis Creek to Wilton Street) adds widened bike lanes with green paint at conflict points.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: BCDCOG Rethink Folly Road Appendix (urban design analysis); Live 5 News, 'Parts of Rethink Folly Road project removed after Town of James Island opts out of agreement' (July 9, 2026)
verifiedClaims.note: Suggested: 'Folly Road is a popular cycling route — it carries bike lanes for much of its length and across the Folly River bridges, but the lanes disappear in places'.

verifiedClaims.claim: The limited shoulder width and inconsistent sidewalk coverage put vulnerable road users in close proximity to high-speed traffic.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: 'Today, Folly road struggles with inefficient traffic operations, infrequent sidewalks, limited bike lanes' (City of Charleston, Rethink Folly Road); the BCDCOG photo inventory labels the 'Five lane section of Folly Rd. No pedestrian infrastructure within the public or private space.' SCDOT counted 15 pedestrian and 21 bicycle crashes on the corridor in 2018-2022.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: City of Charleston, Rethink Folly Road: A Complete Streets Study (snippet); BCDCOG Appendix; SCDOT Board 1 crash history

verifiedClaims.claim: James Island is low-lying and flood-prone. Folly Road floods regularly during heavy rain and king tides, creating hazardous driving conditions — standing water, reduced visibility, and hydroplaning. Crashes during and immediately after flooding events are common.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: Flooding is sourced: 'At times of heavy rain, many storm drains prove inadequate for the storm water generated in the area' (Town comp plan); the Post and Courier reported floodwater on 'James Island's primary streets, including Camp and Folly roads' after an April 2017 rain-at-high-tide event; the City is spending $4.5M on James Island drainage for a neighborhood that floods 'particularly when heavy rainfall coincides with high tides' (Live 5, Sept. 21, 2026). No source supports 'Crashes during and immediately after flooding events are common.'
verifiedClaims.sourceName: Town of James Island Comprehensive Plan 2021; Post and Courier, 'Here's what you need to know about flooding in Charleston as thunderstorm season approaches' (2017); Live 5 News, 'Charleston set to approve $4.5M drainage work, road closures on James Island' (Sept. 21, 2026)
verifiedClaims.note: Keep the first two sentences; drop the last sentence ('Crashes during and immediately after flooding events are common.').

verifiedClaims.claim: Folly Road and Maybank Highway intersection — one of the busiest intersections on James Island, where traffic from Johns Island merges with Folly Road traffic; complex signal timing and heavy turning movements make this a crash hotspot
verifiedClaims.currentValue: Busy: yes — BCDCOG calls it 'the often-congested Maybank Highway/Folly Road intersection', Maybank Highway carried 32,500 vehicles a day at the Stono Bridge in 2019 (Johns Island traffic), and the City retimed the Folly/Maybank signals in 2025. 'Crash hotspot': no intersection-level crash count is published; the intersection is the northern limit of SCDOT's safety-audit corridor.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: BCDCOG Riverland Corridor Management Plan; Town of James Island Comprehensive Plan 2021, Fig. 3.7.1; City of Charleston Traffic and Transportation Committee minutes, Dec. 16, 2025 (30 signals retimed at Maybank Highway and Folly Road; snippet)
verifiedClaims.note: Replace 'make this a crash hotspot' with 'and it marks the northern end of the five-mile stretch SCDOT singled out for its safety audit'. Consider retitling the H2 from 'The Most Dangerous Sections of Folly Road' to 'Where Folly Road's Conflict Points Are' — none of the five bullets has a published crash ranking.

verifiedClaims.claim: Folly Road near Camp Road — the commercial core of James Island with dense driveways, high pedestrian activity, and constant turning conflicts
verifiedClaims.currentValue: Camp Road is in the commercial district; Charleston County rebuilt the Folly Road/Camp Road intersection with half-cent sales tax funds (added turn lanes on Folly and Camp, realigned Eugene Gibbs Street and Rivers Point Row, bike lanes, sidewalks, mast-arm signals with pedestrian signals and brick crosswalks); the County held the ribbon cutting on Aug. 31, 2026.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: Town of James Island Comprehensive Plan 2021 (Folly Road/Camp Road half-cent sales tax project); Charleston County news release, 'Ribbon Cutting Ceremony held for the Folly Road at Camp Road Intersection Improvements Project' (Aug. 31, 2026; snippet)
verifiedClaims.note: Optional freshness add: 'Charleston County finished rebuilding the Folly Road/Camp Road intersection — new turn lanes, mast-arm signals, crosswalks, bike lanes and sidewalks — with half-cent sales tax money in 2026.'

verifiedClaims.claim: The James Island Connector merge — where the high-speed connector (SC-30) feeds into Folly Road, creating speed differential hazards as highway-speed traffic meets surface-street congestion
verifiedClaims.currentValue: 'SC 30/James Island Connector is a four-lane divided limited-access highway that connects the City of Charleston peninsula at Lockwood Drive and Calhoun Street to James Island at SC 171/Folly Road.' Folly Road's highest traffic count (33,000/day in 2019) is at Harbor View Road, beside the Connector interchange.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: City of Charleston, James Island Connector Bicycle Safety Analysis (snippet); Town of James Island Comprehensive Plan 2021, Fig. 3.7.1

verifiedClaims.claim: Folly Road approaching the Folly River bridge — the road narrows and traffic compresses as it approaches the bridge to Folly Beach, creating tailgating and rear-end collision risks
verifiedClaims.currentValue: 'This segment of the corridor transitions from five vehicular lanes (two in each direction and a center turn lane) to one lane in each direction through the conservation area. The bridges to Folly Beach have recently been rebuilt ... and retain one vehicular lane each direction.'
verifiedClaims.sourceName: BCDCOG Rethink Folly Road Appendix (urban design analysis)
verifiedClaims.note: The narrowing is verified; the crash-risk clause is inference and is fine as written.

verifiedClaims.claim: Sol Legare Road intersection — a rural intersection that catches drivers off guard in the transition from commercial to residential sections
verifiedClaims.currentValue: Sol Legare Road is the southern end of the Rethink Folly sidewalk/path segments (segment 5 runs 'Rafeal Lane to Sol Legare Road') and the point where the corridor enters the conservation area; the historic Sol Legare neighborhood lies there. No crash record for the intersection is published, so 'catches drivers off guard' is unsupported.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: BCDCOG Rethink Folly Road Appendix; Charleston County, Rethink Folly Next Steps presentation (Jan. 17, 2018)
verifiedClaims.note: Suggested: 'Sol Legare Road intersection — where the five-lane commercial corridor gives way to the two-lane marsh section, so drivers still carrying 45 mph meet turning traffic from the Sol Legare neighborhood'.

verifiedClaims.claim: The most frequent crash type on Folly Road. Stop-and-go traffic, sudden braking for red lights, and congestion backups — particularly during beach traffic — create conditions where distracted or following-too-closely drivers rear-end the vehicle ahead. Summer weekends see the highest concentration of rear-end crashes.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: No crash-type breakdown for Folly Road is published (SCDOT's audit reports 2,103 vehicular crashes without a manner-of-collision split; its stated concern was angle crashes). Countywide, 'Distracted/Inattention' (2,965) and 'Followed Too Closely' (2,532) were the second- and third-most-listed contributing factors in Charleston County's 2024 collisions, behind failure to yield (3,525). The Fact Book gives no seasonal split; the county's collisions peaked 3-6 p.m. (3,983 of 15,802).
verifiedClaims.sourceName: SCDPS Traffic Collision Fact Book 2024 Edition, Charleston County p. 104 (Top 5 Contributing Factors; Collisions by Time of Day)
verifiedClaims.note: Suggested: 'One of the most common crash types on Folly Road. ... Distraction and following too closely were listed on nearly 5,500 Charleston County crash reports in 2024 (SCDPS Fact Book 2024).' Drop 'Summer weekends see the highest concentration of rear-end crashes.'

verifiedClaims.claim: Cyclists sharing Folly Road with motor vehicles and pedestrians crossing at unsignalized locations are at high risk. The narrow shoulders and absence of protected bike lanes on most of Folly Road mean that bicycle accidents on this corridor tend to be severe.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: SCDOT's road safety audit counted 15 pedestrian and 21 bicycle crashes on the corridor from January 2018 to December 2022, and three of the corridor's six fatal crashes were pedestrian crashes. Countywide in 2024, crashes injured or killed 175 pedestrians (13 killed) and 116 bicyclists (4 killed).
verifiedClaims.sourceName: SCDOT, SC 171 Folly Road Road Safety Audit, Board 1 Crash History; SCDPS Fact Book 2024, Charleston County p. 105 (Vulnerable Roadway Users)
verifiedClaims.note: Suggested addition after the second sentence: 'SCDOT's safety audit counted 21 bicycle and 15 pedestrian crashes on the corridor between 2018 and 2022, and three of its six fatal crashes killed pedestrians.' Keep the internal links.

verifiedClaims.claim: DUI crashes cluster on Folly Road because it is the primary route home from Folly Beach's bars and restaurants. Late-night and early-morning DUI crashes — particularly during summer and holidays — produce some of the most severe injuries on the corridor.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: No source shows DUI crashes clustering on Folly Road; SCDOT's audit and the SCDPS Fact Book publish no DUI count by road. Sourced substitutes: Folly Road is the only road off Folly Beach; statewide, an alcohol-impaired driver was involved in 40% of South Carolina's 2024 traffic deaths (417 of 1,038; SCDPS Fact Book 2024 p. 72, verified in facts-4729); Charleston County's fatal collisions in 2024 were concentrated between 9 p.m. and 3 a.m. (20 of 57).
verifiedClaims.sourceName: SCDPS Traffic Collision Fact Book 2024 Edition, p. 72 (alcohol-impaired driving fatalities) and Charleston County p. 104 (time of day)
verifiedClaims.note: Suggested: 'Folly Road is the only road home from Folly Beach's bars and restaurants, and impaired drivers are a statewide problem: an alcohol-impaired driver was involved in 40% of South Carolina's traffic deaths in 2024 (SCDPS Fact Book 2024). Twenty of Charleston County's 57 fatal collisions that year happened between 9 p.m. and 3 a.m.' Drop 'cluster' and 'produce some of the most severe injuries on the corridor'.

verifiedClaims.claim: fatal crashes on Folly Road occur multiple times per year, particularly in DUI incidents and high-speed T-bone collisions
verifiedClaims.currentValue: SCDOT recorded six fatal crashes on the audited stretch of Folly Road in the five years from January 2018 to December 2022 — three pedestrian, three vehicular — roughly one a year, not 'multiple times per year'. No DUI or T-bone attribution is published.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: SCDOT, SC 171 Folly Road Road Safety Audit, Board 1 Crash History
verifiedClaims.note: Suggested bullet: 'Wrongful death — SCDOT counted six fatal crashes on Folly Road between 2018 and 2022, half of them pedestrians'. Keep the internal link.

verifiedClaims.claim: Government entities — SCDOT and Charleston County may bear responsibility for road design defects, inadequate signage, missing turn lanes, signal timing issues, or failure to address known crash clusters under the South Carolina Tort Claims Act (S.C. Code § 15-78-10 et seq.)
verifiedClaims.currentValue: § 15-78-10 is the Act's short-title section ('This chapter may be cited as the "South Carolina Tort Claims Act"'), so '§ 15-78-10 et seq.' is a valid citation to the Act as a whole. The operative rules the bullet omits: two years from discovery to sue (§ 15-78-110; three if a verified claim was filed within one year under § 15-78-80); damages capped at $300,000 per person and $600,000 per occurrence with no punitive damages (§ 15-78-120); and the exceptions in § 15-78-60, including (5) discretionary decisions and (15) sign, signal, guardrail or median-barrier defects unless not corrected 'within a reasonable time after actual or constructive notice'. Ownership: 'Folly Road is a South Carolina Department of Transportation (SCDOT) major arterial road ... SCDOT has ownership of the corridor for design, access' (BCDCOG); the City of Charleston maintains SCDOT signals on its sections; Charleston County builds intersection projects with sales-tax funds.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: S.C. Code §§ 15-78-10, 15-78-60, 15-78-80, 15-78-110, 15-78-120; BCDCOG Rethink Folly Road Appendix B.12; Charleston City James Island Intergovernmental Council agenda, July 30, 2025 (SCDOT light maintained by the City; snippet)
verifiedClaims.note: Suggested: 'Government entities — Folly Road is an SCDOT-owned state highway, the City of Charleston maintains many of its signals, and Charleston County builds its intersection projects, so any of them may answer for a design defect, a signal or sign left uncorrected after notice, or a missing turn lane under the South Carolina Tort Claims Act (S.C. Code § 15-78-10 et seq.). Those claims carry a two-year deadline (§ 15-78-110), a cap of $300,000 per person and $600,000 per occurrence with no punitive damages (§ 15-78-120), and immunity for discretionary decisions (§ 15-78-60).' Mirror the two-year point in the Filing Deadlines section and in faq:2.

verifiedClaims.claim: Bars and restaurants — under South Carolina's dram shop law (S.C. Code § 61-2-145), establishments on Folly Beach that serve visibly intoxicated patrons who then cause a DUI crash on Folly Road may share liability
verifiedClaims.currentValue: § 61-2-145 is not a dram-shop law. It is the liquor liability insurance mandate: an on-premises licensee open after 5 p.m. 'is required to maintain a liquor liability insurance policy ... of at least one million dollars' (the 2026 version adds a risk-mitigation-program alternative in subsection (E)). South Carolina has no dram-shop act; server liability is negligence per se on the criminal sale statutes — § 61-4-580(A)(2) (a beer/wine permittee may not 'knowingly ... sell beer or wine to an intoxicated person') and § 61-6-2220 (liquor licensees 'may not sell these beverages to persons in an intoxicated condition'; 'knowingly' from 2026) — recognized in Tobias v. Sports Club, Inc. (S.C. 1998) and Hartfield v. Getaway Lounge & Grill, Inc., 388 S.C. 407 (2010). For claims arising after January 1, 2026, § 61-2-147 makes a licensee jointly and severally liable for 50% of actual damages when a verdict is returned against both it and a driver charged under §§ 56-5-2930, -2933 or -2945.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: S.C. Code § 61-2-145 (both versions), § 61-2-147, § 61-4-580, § 61-6-2220; analysis reused from facts-4729
verifiedClaims.note: Suggested: 'Bars and restaurants — South Carolina has no dram-shop act, but an establishment that knowingly serves a visibly intoxicated patron violates S.C. Code §§ 61-4-580 and 61-6-2220, and the courts treat that as negligence per se (Tobias v. Sports Club; Hartfield v. Getaway Lounge & Grill). A Folly Beach bar that over-serves a driver who then crashes on Folly Road may share liability.' The next paragraph on the 2025 Act already carries § 61-2-147. Same correction in faq:4. Statute URLs: t61c004.php (§ 61-4-580), t61c006.php (§ 61-6-2220), t61c002.php (§ 61-2-147). Case links (CourtListener, from facts-4729): Tobias https://www.courtlistener.com/opinion/1358670/tobias-v-sports-club-inc/ ; Hartfield https://www.courtlistener.com/opinion/1347026/hartfield-v-getaway-lounge-grill-inc/ — cite by name only unless the host is added to the allowlist.

verifiedClaims.claim: South Carolina changed these rules for claims arising after 1 January 2026. The 2025 Act narrowed the alcohol exception in S.C. Code § 15-38-15 and created § 61-2-147, under which an establishment can be jointly and severally liable for fifty percent of a plaintiff’s actual damages where a verdict is returned against both it and a driver charged with DUI
verifiedClaims.currentValue: 2025 Act No. 42 (H.3430), effective January 1, 2026, 'applies only to causes of action or claims arising or accruing after January 1, 2026'. The 2026 version of § 15-38-15 is retitled 'willful or reckless defendant and drug exceptions' — the 'alcoholic beverage' exception is gone from the title. § 61-2-147(A): 'If a verdict is rendered against both a licensee and a defendant charged under Section 56-5-2930, 56-5-2933, or 56-5-2945, then the licensee is jointly and severally liable for fifty percent of the plaintiff's actual damages.' The internal link /resources/south-carolina-liquor-liability-2026/ resolves (title 'What South Carolina's 2026 Liquor Liability Law Changed').
verifiedClaims.sourceName: S.C. Code § 61-2-147; § 15-38-15 (versions effective until and from Jan. 1, 2026); rodenlaw.com resource page
verifiedClaims.note: Accurate; reused from facts-4729 and re-read on scstatehouse.gov this run.

verifiedClaims.claim: South Carolina follows a modified comparative fault rule (Nelson v. Concrete Supply Co.). You can recover damages if your fault is less than 51%. Your recovery is reduced by your percentage of fault.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: Nelson v. Concrete Supply Co., 303 S.C. 243, 399 S.E.2d 783 (1991): plaintiff recovers if their negligence is not greater than the defendant's (the 51% bar), reduced by their share.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: Nelson v. Concrete Supply Co. (S.C. 1991), Justia; writer-profile jurisdiction table
verifiedClaims.note: Correct authority. Never substitute § 15-38-15 for the plaintiff's bar.

verifiedClaims.claim: Georgia, where Roden Law also practices, applies a slightly stricter threshold — recovery is barred at 50% or more fault (O.C.G.A. § 51-12-33).
verifiedClaims.currentValue: The Georgia rule is stated correctly, but this is a South Carolina-only hyperlocal post (Folly Road, Charleston County, Charleston office). The writer profile's jurisdiction rule: cross-jurisdiction law on a single-state page is an error. Remove the paragraph.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: profiles/writer-profile.md, Jurisdiction rules
verifiedClaims.note: Delete the whole paragraph; nothing else in the section depends on it.

verifiedClaims.claim: South Carolina provides three years from the date of the accident for personal injury claims (S.C. Code § 15-3-530) and three years from the date of death for wrongful death claims (S.C. Code § 15-51-20).
verifiedClaims.currentValue: § 15-3-530(5): three years for 'any injury to the person'; § 15-3-530(6): three years for 'an action under Sections 15-51-10 to 15-51-60 for death by wrongful act, the period to begin to run upon the death of the person'. § 15-51-20 is the wrongful-death section (action 'brought by or in the name of the executor or administrator'), so citing it beside the death claim is fine; the three-year period itself sits in § 15-3-530(6).
verifiedClaims.note: Add one sentence: 'A claim against SCDOT, the City of Charleston or Charleston County under the Tort Claims Act must be filed within two years (S.C. Code § 15-78-110).'

verifiedClaims.claim: Critical evidence on Folly Road disappears quickly — traffic camera footage, business surveillance video, and vehicle data are all time-sensitive.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: General practice statement with no figure.

verifiedClaims.claim: Seek medical attention — even seemingly minor symptoms can indicate serious injury; document everything within 24 hours

verifiedClaims.claim: Folly Road is James Island's primary corridor and one of Charleston's most crash-prone roads due to heavy traffic, limited turn lanes, and dense commercial development.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: 'Limited turn lanes' is wrong — the James Island section has a continuous center turn lane, and the problem SCDOT identified is uncontrolled left turns across it. The crash-prone characterization is supported by SCDOT's 2018-2022 count (2,103 vehicle crashes, 525 injury, 6 fatal on five miles).
verifiedClaims.sourceName: SCDOT SC 171 Folly Road Safety Audit handout; BCDCOG Rethink Folly Road Appendix
verifiedClaims.note: Suggested: 'Folly Road is James Island's primary corridor and one of Charleston's most crash-prone roads — SCDOT counted 2,103 vehicle crashes on five miles of it from 2018 to 2022 — because of heavy traffic, uncontrolled left turns across its center turn lane, and dense commercial driveways.'

verifiedClaims.claim: Liable parties may include other drivers, the City of Charleston, or SCDOT for road design deficiencies.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: SCDOT owns Folly Road; the City of Charleston maintains signals on its sections; Charleston County builds intersection projects. Claims run under the Tort Claims Act with a two-year deadline and $300,000/$600,000 caps.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: BCDCOG Rethink Folly Road Appendix B.12; S.C. Code §§ 15-78-110, 15-78-120

verifiedClaims.currentValue: § 15-3-530(5); Nelson v. Concrete Supply Co.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: S.C. Code § 15-3-530; Nelson v. Concrete Supply Co. (S.C. 1991)

verifiedClaims.claim: What makes Folly Road one of Charleston's most crash-prone corridors, and your options after a collision on James Island.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: Supported by SCDOT's selection of the corridor through the federal Highway Safety Improvement Program, which targets 'locations throughout the state with high crash rates or patterns', and the 2,103-crash count.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: SCDOT SC 171 Folly Road Safety Audit handout (May 22, 2025)
verifiedClaims.note: Also the Article description in schema; no change.

verifiedClaims.claim: Folly Road is the only route between James Island, downtown Charleston, and Folly Beach, concentrating all traffic onto a single corridor.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: It is the only road to Folly Beach. It is not the only route between James Island and downtown: Harbor View Road feeds the James Island Connector, and Maybank Highway/Wappoo Cut and Riverland Drive carry island traffic to West Ashley and the peninsula.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: BCDCOG Riverland Corridor Management Plan; City of Charleston, James Island Connector Bicycle Safety Analysis (snippet)
verifiedClaims.note: FAQPage structured data. Suggested: 'Folly Road is the only road on and off Folly Beach and James Island's main commercial spine, so beach traffic and local traffic share one five-lane corridor.'

verifiedClaims.claim: It combines high-volume commuter traffic with tourist beach traffic, dense commercial driveways, frequent speed limit changes, limited shoulders for cyclists and pedestrians, and regular flooding. During summer months the traffic volume surges dramatically, making rear-end collisions and left-turn crashes especially common.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: 'Frequent speed limit changes' is not supported (45 mph across most of James Island, dropping at Folly Beach); the rest is consistent with the Town comp plan and BCDCOG study. 'Making rear-end collisions and left-turn crashes especially common' has no seasonal source; SCDOT's audit identified angle (left-turn) crashes as the severe-injury pattern.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: BCDCOG Rethink Folly Road Appendix; Town of James Island Comprehensive Plan 2021; WCIV May 22, 2025 (SCDOT on angle crashes)
verifiedClaims.note: Suggested: 'It combines commuter traffic with beach traffic, dense commercial driveways, a 45 mph limit that drops sharply at Folly Beach, limited shoulders for cyclists and pedestrians, and flooding in heavy rain. SCDOT counted 2,103 vehicle crashes on five miles of it between 2018 and 2022, and its safety audit singled out left-turn angle crashes as the ones that injure and kill.'

verifiedClaims.claim: Move to safety if possible since secondary crashes are a real risk on this busy road. Call 911 for police and medical assistance. Seek medical attention within 24 hours even if symptoms seem minor.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: Practical guidance; no legal figure.

verifiedClaims.claim: South Carolina allows three years from the date of the accident for personal injury claims (S.C. Code section 15-3-530) and three years from the date of death for wrongful death claims.
verifiedClaims.note: Add: 'A claim against SCDOT, the City of Charleston or Charleston County must be filed within two years (S.C. Code section 15-78-110).'

verifiedClaims.claim: However, critical evidence like traffic camera footage and business surveillance video is typically overwritten within 30-72 hours, so contacting a lawyer within the first few days is essential.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: No source supports a 30-72-hour retention figure; retention varies by system and operator.
verifiedClaims.note: FAQPage structured data. Suggested: 'However, business surveillance video and traffic camera footage are often overwritten within days, so contacting a lawyer quickly is essential.'

verifiedClaims.claim: South Carolina follows a modified comparative fault rule (Nelson v. Concrete Supply Co.) that allows recovery as long as your fault is less than 51 percent. Your compensation is reduced by your percentage of fault.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: Nelson v. Concrete Supply Co., 303 S.C. 243 (1991).
verifiedClaims.sourceName: Nelson v. Concrete Supply Co. (S.C. 1991), Justia

verifiedClaims.claim: Potentially, yes. Under South Carolina's dram shop law (S.C. Code section 61-2-145), bars and restaurants can be held liable if they serve alcohol to a visibly intoxicated person who then causes a DUI crash.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: § 61-2-145 is the $1 million liquor-liability insurance requirement, not a dram-shop law, and South Carolina has no dram-shop act. Liability is negligence per se under §§ 61-4-580 and 61-6-2220 (knowing sale to an intoxicated person), recognized in Tobias v. Sports Club (1998) and Hartfield v. Getaway Lounge & Grill (2010); for crashes after January 1, 2026, § 61-2-147 makes the licensee jointly and severally liable for 50% of actual damages when a verdict is returned against both it and a driver charged with DUI.
verifiedClaims.note: FAQPage structured data. Suggested: 'Potentially, yes. South Carolina has no dram-shop act, but a bar or restaurant that knowingly serves a visibly intoxicated patron violates S.C. Code sections 61-4-580 and 61-6-2220, and the courts treat that as negligence per se (Tobias v. Sports Club; Hartfield v. Getaway Lounge & Grill). For crashes after January 1, 2026, section 61-2-147 can make the establishment jointly liable for half of your actual damages when a verdict is returned against both it and the DUI driver. Folly Road is the only road home from Folly Beach's bars, which makes over-service a live question in DUI crashes on this corridor.'

verifiedClaims.claim: T-bone collisions at intersections and high-speed rear-end crashes tend to produce the most severe injuries. Pedestrian and bicycle crashes on Folly Road are also disproportionately severe due to the lack of protected infrastructure.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: SCDOT: angle crashes 'tend to result in the most severe accidents' on this corridor; three of the corridor's six fatal crashes in 2018-2022 were pedestrian crashes, out of 15 pedestrian crashes — which supports 'disproportionately severe' with a number.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: Count On 2, May 13, 2025 (SCDOT's Shawn Salley); SCDOT Board 1 Crash History
verifiedClaims.note: FAQPage structured data. Suggested last sentence: 'Pedestrian and bicycle crashes on Folly Road are disproportionately severe: three of the corridor's six fatal crashes between 2018 and 2022 killed pedestrians, according to SCDOT's road safety audit.'
